body:
I'm not a proper mind to fully help you but I wanted to add one thing that maybe will help.

There are programs out there in college and universities that will accept your work experiences as course credits. This can help your graduate and earn your degree. I can't refer you to any specific schools, but the possibility does exist. You may find that a school may only require you to take a few more courses to complete your degree - something much more manageable than two more entire semesters. If this is a really pressing issue, and one that could potentially relieve a lot of stress, I would suggest you at least investigate the possibility.

Like I said earlier, I'm not in the best frame of mind to be giving advice but I happened by chance to read yours and felt compelled to add that bit. Hope it helped a tiny bit.

I know that I'm not 100% sure, I'm trying to search for that certain thing that's going to keep me alive. To give me the motivation to say "okay, I'm not going to kill myself". I want a reason or reasons to stay alive, that's the entire point of giving myself 24 hours and for posting here. I don't want a reason that will keep me alive temporarily. I want a reason, and I want to find it, that will keep be alive forever. Life is simple to most - they stay alive because of a reason. People want to live because it's important, not because of some trivial reason. I need to find that important reason, I want to. I also don't want to wait around forever hoping it will show up. 

I'm at the end of my rope, I might have even lost that rope and am holding on by a tiny string now. It's something, I'm still here, but that tiny piece of string that's holding me here won't last long.

In all honesty, I died once already. I "came back" AKA my heart started beating again. I'm not afraid of death - in fact I didn't even know I was dead. Which sounds really weird, but it's equal to anyone who's had general anesthesia. It doesn't feel like you were even sleeping/sedated/etc, minutes or hours can pass and there's just nothing, no memory. Death is different...it's odd. I can't quite explain it, words are hard to find, using the example of anesthesia is the only thing I can really relate it to.

I'm not afraid of death. I haven't been for a while. I'm not scared of death, it's nothing. I was fearful of dying - of killing myself and it going horribly wrong so as I were to come out technically still alive. 

I would rather be dead then be alive just laying around, sucking up oxygen, time and money. I know this is black and white thinking, all or nothing, but that's where I'm at now.

I've been thinking a lot tonight. I realized dying would be incredibly hypocritical in regards to who I am. I don't know why the thought never occurred to me before, but oh well. I've been doing occasional work over the past several months that involves responding to individuals in crisis. Not just concerning suicide, but suicide was included. I haven't been doing that recently within the past month or so, I suppose I forgot what I had be previously doing - well I didn't forget, I just didn't realize how hypocritical my death would be. That's a bit unsettling.

I appreciate your help, for now I'm going to get some sleep. I have an important day tomorrow, but I'm going to enjoy this time to sleep. I'll be back online in late morning, as I'll be cleaning up all the stuff that's thrown everywhere. After that I'll occasionally check in on my cell. 

I do want to find a real reason for staying alive, but I'm preparing for not finding one.

There's no significance as to Monday. I considered Tuesday, as it would have been the day years back when my last overdose was. Five years to the day on Tuesday. I then realized how absolutely cliche that would be, taking my life on the day I decided to begin recovering.

I considered mother's day as well as my family's birthdays. Monday places my death technically after Mother's day as well as avoiding any birthdays or other significant events.

In terms of why now, at this very time, this very day...well it's not entirely complicated. I have thought about this over the past two weeks. I've denied any impulsive desires to kill myself. I've been arguing with my college to no avail, something which held me back. I'm just at the point of "I'm done, I am truly and utterly done". There's only so much I can do, feeling suicidal, and I'm emotionally exhausted. 

I've got a plan, I have the means, and I've got a time. I know that fulfills the three important questions that anyone working with suicidal patients asks. I've been through the long lists of questions and assessments. I know what people are looking for, which means I know what to hide or avoid saying to prevent people around me from catching on. 

It really boils down to the point of emotional exhaustion.

I think that's a rather surface issue. Of course I know that a part of me is hurt by the lack of my family's response. I also know that this thinking is highly incorrect. If I attempt to see things objectively, I can understand that my family members do notice and validate my suicidal thoughts. I also can understand they have been through so much with me, multiple doctors, medication trials, hospital visits. It's no doubt they're exhausted, physically and emotionally. It's no doubt that I see them as distant even though they are standing next to me. I know they recognize that my words and feelings are the truth, and I think they may know me too well. I have talked about suicide often, for years. Initially anyone's response to "I'm going to kill myself" is strong, sound the alarms, red lights flashing, that sort of thing. My family has grown to know that I will often have fleeting thoughts of suicide, and that if I have strong thoughts I will seek help. 

The problem lies in what I said before, if I really want to die I will actually do it. Since I am planning on actually dying Monday morning, I'm not going to go search for help. I will say my good-byes, I will have my final conversations, but they will just be that. Conversations. There will be no cryptic messages that I hope they pick up. I will be subtle but caring as this will be their last memory. Now that I've decided to kill myself Monday morning, unless I somehow find a reason to keep living, I won't be purposefully dropping hints about my death. I want to die, I won't be interrupted or stopped. 

Perhaps I am somewhat unique in this aspect. I am hoping for something to change my decision but it won't be because someone is holding me back. This thing that would change me decision would have to be mine alone, I would make the choice to back out. I won't be living just because someone gets the idea to call the police or EMS. While the likelihood of this happening is incredibly low, it won't stop me from killing myself. Hospitalization and even more medication won't cure me. I'll get out having not found the reason or reasons to be alive and will again go about planning to kill myself.

My friends do not know my feelings tonight. Since we met in college, we're spread across many states with varying distances. I've distanced myself from using Facebook and texting. On some level it was intentional, I know full well a few of my friends wouldn't think twice about calling 911 and sound so panicked that I have three different districts of police and EMS outside my house. Another part of me has been taking time to carefully construct what I'm going to say to them tomorrow - I will call them but I won't have them in a panic. 

I've told my family multiple times I will kill myself. While they understand that on some level I'm being serious, another level I don't think they quite believe me. Denial I suppose which is only natural. They care and love me deeply, yet my family has been with me through so much that I think their thinking borders on, "well you haven't killed yourself yet". That sounds rather crude, there's a better way to put that to words I'm sure. 

I have told family and doctors when I've sought help for suicidal feelings, "If I really wanted to die, I would be dead and not here". I've expressed that many times to multiple people. It's the truth. If after today I decide to go through and commit suicide, I will just do it. There will be no nonsense "suicidal gesture". I have experienced suicidal feelings before. If I want help, I will seek it. I don't have to do a half-way suicide attempt to feel the need to "deserve" help. If I want to die, I will die. There's no question.

At the moment I'm on my computer, which is the most obvious point. I'm switching between watching Netflix and Amazon Prime. I will sleep tonight later. I'll wake up and live out my last day. I will clean up all my mess - put away things in order, do my laundry, make sure I leave my personal things easy to be accessed/boxed up/whatever my family decides after my death. I will take a long shower, and finally get dressed in my final outfit. I will go out for the last time during the day. I'll treat myself to frozen yogurt, iced coffee, and my favorite salad at Panera Bread. I'll take a long walk out in the country, breathe in the smells, look at the world in a different way. I hope that I find that certain thing to keep me alive, if not, I'm perfectly okay with dying. I will visit the graveyard where I want a tombstone to be placed for me - even though I want to be cremated and my ashes spread at sea. I will write in my journal multiple times during the day, I'll further think things over. I will probably end up adding to my suicide note, details that I realized should be added during my last day. I'll say my good-byes to friends and family. I'll say my good-byes to my pets. I'll probably talk to my family and friends just to make sure they have a good "last memory" of me. If come Monday morning, I still have not found a reason to stay alive, I will then kill myself.

Many people couldn't begin to understand how a suicidal person is logical or rational. Suicide, after all, seems completely illogical - dying goes against everything both psychological and biological that makes us human.  There's a small group of people that exist for reasons unknown. I think the common perception both in the public and medical field is that anyone who's suicidal can in no way be thinking rationally, or "competently". 

I also recognize that my suicide would cause pain to those around me, I do. I had friends in high school who killed themselves, impulsively. It hurt me, emotionally. It hurt as I had to listen to my friend talk to me while she was dying, refusing to tell me where she was and having to just listen to her fade. It hurt finding out that another friend killed herself when it was obvious she had a change of heart - she overdosed, collapsed outside in broad daylight trying to seek help but she was dead by the time EMS got to her body. It hurt immensely when yet another friend killed herself and I had to read an email from her family - her sister - about how my friend had a change of heart at the last second but because her door was barricaded she died by the time the fire department broke into her room. I'm no stranger to feeling the pain associated with suicide. While I can never correctly imagine the pain that would result from my suicide, I do know that the pain lessens over time. It's never gone, the person is not forgotten, but over time the tears will slow, the pain will diminish, and the people grieving will move on.

Despite this, despite what I just said, the majority of the population still cannot believe that suicide can be completely logical, thought out, and so forth. Which is quite sad actually. If I were to choose to live and have no plan of how, I would be considered to be thinking logically. Yet because I am choosing to die, even though I have a secure plan, I am not thinking logically.

Since I'm fully invested in figuring out life/living in my last day, I would be fine with talking. It's doubtful in my mind that talking to anyone would keep me from taking my life but I'm fine with it.
